newsitem.title: POLAND: Three investors bidding for Polish bank PBI.
newsitem.headline: Three investors bidding for Polish bank PBI.

text.p: Two foreign investors and one domestic investor remain in the running to buy a strategic stake in Polish Investment Bank SA (PBI), the bank's president said in the Nowa Europa daily on Wednesday.
"The battle for (PBI) is being played out between three investors -- two foreign and one Polish," the paper quoted Lech Kurklinski as saying.
No senior officals at the bank were immediately available for comment.

The daily Parkiet quoted Kurklinski as saying that all three entities would likely submit their final offers in February and that PBI needed to double its current own funds. PBI's own funds were at 179 million zlotys at the end of 1995.
The bank has said that the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, would likely choose a strategic investor for PBI by the end of March.

Both PBI and the NBP have refused to confirm press speculation that the central bank had shortlisted three banks bidding for PBI and smaller Prosper Bank SA -- Kredyt Bank, GE Capital and Creditanstalt.
Kredyt Bank is currently in the process of forming a banking group with three other Polish banks and an insurer.
Parkiet said PBI, recently awarded a BBB- long-term rating by IBCA, made a net profit of 54.9 million zlotys last year. In 1995 PBI made a net profit of 26.2 million zlotys.
PBI, carved out of the NBP in 1993 with a clean credit portfolio, remains 100-percent owned by the central bank.
The NBP took control of more than 90 percent of ailing Prosper Bank in 1993 as a result of a bail-out scheme and has since retained its stake to guide the bank's turnaround.
